A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Riemannian Generative Decoder work. All 18 pages of v2 and 21 pages of v3, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on cell-cycle expression data, synthetic branching diffusion, and human mitochondrial DNA, including reconstruction, downstream prediction, generation, ablations, and runtime results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a qualitative phylogenetic tree reconstruction using learned hmtDNA representations in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Decoder-only MAP learning, per-sample manifold latents, Adam/RiemannianAdam optimization, geometric noise, and frozen-decoder test-time inference remain unchanged. The expanded objective and optimization exposition describe the existing procedure; Listing S2 corrects an undefined variable without introducing a new algorithm.

E1.justification: The three original datasets and their coverage are retained. v3 Figure 6 adds a downstream phylogenetic tree-reconstruction task on hmtDNA representations, extending the earlier embedding, correlation, and classification evaluations.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain S-VAE, diffusion VAE, P-VAE, and explicit curvature regularization where previously evaluated. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines. Neighbor joining in Figure 6 processes the proposed model's representations rather than serving as a competing representation method.

E3.justification: The reported Lorentz curvature changes from c = 5.0 in v2 to c = 0.2 in v3, which now identifies geoopt's parameter k = 5.0; this correction does not establish rerunning experiments. Figure 6 adds neighbor joining on pairwise Lorentz distances between 300 sampled representations. Existing splits, architectures, and training budgets remain.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 6 adds a qualitative case study testing whether learned hmtDNA geodesics reconstruct established haplogroup relationships. Existing noise and curvature ablations remain. The training-correlation analysis moves from v2 Figure S5 to v3 Figure 4 without new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-initialization reporting for Tables 1–2, three runs for Table S1, and the same mean-and-standard-deviation practices. Timing measurements across 100 epochs and the training trajectories' five-run reporting, including the single explicit-regularizer run, are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 6 newly reports that a neighbor-joining tree from 300 hmtDNA representations has global structure qualitatively similar to established lineages. All matched quantitative tables retain their numerical values. The generative-fidelity table and training-correlation plot are retained results relocated into the main text.

T1.justification: v3 Equation 16 corrects the missing factor of two multiplying the residual-Hessian sum in v2 Equation 14. The accompanying justification now explicitly assumes the residual contribution is negligible on average. The resulting regularizer and the remaining derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain decoder-only representation learning on arbitrary Riemannian manifolds, scalable geometric noise regularization, interpretable biological representations, and higher-dimensional stability. The added abstract sentence about Euclidean distortion restates existing motivation rather than changing the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes MAP fitting from maximizing a marginal-likelihood lower bound and expands the rationale for choosing geometry from prior knowledge. It removes the blanket assertion of significant training superiority and the footnote dismissing generalization performance. Automatic manifold selection is added as future work; the memory limitation remains.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix B.1 clarify geoopt's Lorentz parameterization, including k = 1/c. Listing S2 replaces undefined x arguments with z. Figure 6 documents its sample count, distance measure, and tree-building procedure. Most hyperparameters, hardware details, and code/data links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds focused comparisons with scPhere, supervised Poincaré embeddings, GAGA, and classical manifold-learning methods. Additional citations support biological topology, phylogenetics, and optimization. These broaden context while retaining the original positioning around avoiding encoder-based manifold-density approximations.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the model-formulation explanation, separates geometric regularization, and moves the manifold overview and selected appendix results into the main narrative. It also edits introductory language and cross-references, adds acknowledgments and broader-impact prose, and removes standalone reproducibility and LLM statements. The overall research narrative remains.

P2.justification: The journal layout substantially changes typography, spacing, and figure placement. Figure 2 becomes an enlarged two-by-two grid, Figure S2 is enlarged and relabeled with k, and Figure 6 is added. The former Figure S5 and Table S2 become main-text displays with text wrapping around them.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical accuracy and reproducibility through the Hessian correction and explicit curvature-to-geoopt parameter mapping. Clearer MAP explanations, better contextual positioning, and enlarged visualizations improve accessibility. The added tree example supplies limited qualitative support; the unchanged quantitative evidence makes the overall gain modest.
